_: GutLog v3.19.0, the monthly medicine order. Every assertion below is about
behaviour v3.18.0 did not have -- it had no order, no pack form and no
order routes -- so each fails against the reconstructed v3.18.0.
Three of them are also the ones that would be cheapest to get wrong while
still passing, so they are controlled by a deliberate break of v3.19.0
instead, which is the stronger control:
03  ordering a flat target instead of a top-up
04  forgetting what a filled pillbox still holds
13  the order plan served without a login

assertions.name: 01 bad pack, days, order and receipt calls are refused
02 the order counts from the stock expected on the 1st, in whole packs
03 the order is a top-up to the target, never a flat month

mutation.why: order the whole target every month, ignoring stock on hand, and see the top-up assertion catch it

assertions.name: 04 filling the pillbox does not change the order

mutation.why: forget the days a filled pillbox still holds, and see the invariant catch it
mutation.find: expected = r["current"] + use * in_box - use * gap

assertions.name: 05 an SOS medicine is topped up to its keep-on-hand figure
06 a medicine with no schedule and no keep is ordered from its use
07 what cannot be ordered is named with the reason
08 a medicine stopping before the 1st is not ordered
09 sending saves the order once for the month
10 order received adds to stock, once, and undoes cleanly
12 the due window is the last seven days of the month
13 the order routes refuse without a login

mutation.why: take @login_required off /api/order and see the assertion catch it

assertions.name: 14 Python 3.9 syntax, Jinja-clean JS, page renders the order card
